title: In-Sync: Adaptation of Speech Aware Large Language Models for ASR with Word Level Timestamp Predictions
comment: Accepted to ICASSP 2026
summary: Recent advances in speech-aware language models have coupled strong acoustic encoders with large language models, enabling systems that move beyond transcription to produce richer outputs. Among these, word-level timestamp prediction is critical for applications such as captioning, media search, and multimodal synchronization, yet it is often handled by external alignment tools. In this work, we extend an existing speech-aware language model to predict timestamps directly alongside transcripts. We introduce a set of novel lightweight training strategies that improve alignment robustness while preserving recognition quality. Experiments across multiple datasets show that these strategies not only enhance timestamp accuracy, but also yield gains in overall ASR performance. Together, they demonstrate an efficient and unified approach to speech recognition with precise timestamp prediction.

AI.tldr: This paper extends a speech-aware language model to directly predict word-level timestamps alongside transcripts using lightweight training strategies that improve alignment robustness and ASR performance.
AI.motivation: Word-level timestamp prediction is critical for applications like captioning, media search, and multimodal synchronization, but is often handled by external alignment tools rather than integrated into the speech recognition model itself.
AI.method: The authors extend an existing speech-aware language model to predict timestamps directly alongside transcripts, and introduce novel lightweight training strategies that improve alignment robustness while preserving recognition quality.
AI.result: Experiments across multiple datasets show that the proposed strategies enhance timestamp accuracy and yield gains in overall ASR performance.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides an efficient and unified solution for speech recognition with precise timestamp prediction.

title: Predictive Directional Selective Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control for Moving Sources via a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network
summary: Directional Selective Fixed-Filter Active Noise Control (D-SFANC) can effectively attenuate noise from different directions by selecting the suitable pre-trained control filter based on the Direction-of-Arrival (DoA) of the current noise. However, this method is weak at tracking the direction variations of non-stationary noise, such as that from a moving source. Therefore, this work proposes a Predictive Directional SFANC (PD-SFANC) method that uses a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) to capture the hidden temporal dynamics of the moving noise and predict the control filter to cancel future noise. Accordingly, the proposed method can significantly improve its noise-tracking ability and dynamic noise-reduction performance. Furthermore, numerical simulations confirm the superiority of the proposed method for handling moving sources across various movement scenarios, compared to several representative ANC baselines.

AI.tldr: PD-SFANC uses a CRNN to predict control filters for moving noise sources, improving upon D-SFANC by tracking direction variations in non-stationary noise for better active noise control.
AI.motivation: D-SFANC is weak at tracking direction variations of non-stationary noise (e.g., moving sources), limiting its dynamic noise-reduction performance.
AI.method: Proposes Predictive Directional SFANC (PD-SFANC) that employs a Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network (CRNN) to capture temporal dynamics of moving noise and predict the appropriate control filter for future noise cancellation.
AI.result: Numerical simulations show PD-SFANC outperforms representative ANC baselines across various moving source scenarios, with significantly improved noise-tracking ability and dynamic noise reduction.
AI.conclusion: PD-SFANC effectively enhances directional active noise control for non-stationary moving sources by leveraging CRNN-based prediction of control filters.

title: Explainable AI in Speaker Recognition -- Making Latent Representations Understandable
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures
summary: Neural networks can be trained to learn task-relevant representations from data. Understanding how these networks make decisions falls within the Explainable AI (XAI) domain. This paper proposes to study an XAI topic: uncovering unknown organisational patterns in network representations, particularly those representations learned by the speaker recognition network that recognises the speaker identity of utterances. Past studies employed algorithms (e.g. t-distributed Stochastic Neighbour Embedding and K-means) to analyse and visualise how network representations form independent clusters, indicating the presence of flat clustering phenomena within the space defined by these representations. In contrast, this work applies two algorithms -- Single-Linkage Clustering (SLINK) and Hierarchical Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (HDBSCAN) -- to analyse how representations form clusters with hierarchical relationships rather than being independent, thereby demonstrating the existence of hierarchical clustering phenomena within the network representation space. To semantically understand the above hierarchical clustering phenomena, a new algorithm, termed Hierarchical Cluster-Class Matching (HCCM), is designed to perform one-to-one matching between predefined semantic classes and hierarchical representation clusters (i.e. those produced by SLINK or HDBSCAN). Some hierarchical clusters are successfully matched to individual semantic classes (e.g. male, UK), while others to conjunctions of semantic classes (e.g. male and UK, female and Ireland). A new metric, Liebig's score, is proposed to quantify the performance of each matching behaviour, allowing us to diagnose the factor that most strongly limits matching performance.

AI.tldr: This paper applies hierarchical clustering algorithms (SLINK and HDBSCAN) to speaker recognition network representations, revealing hierarchical rather than flat clustering phenomena. A new Hierarchical Cluster-Class Matching (HCCM) algorithm matches clusters to semantic classes (single or conjunctive), and Liebig's score quantifies matching performance to identify limiting factors.
AI.motivation: Existing XAI studies on network representations have only identified flat clustering phenomena (using t-SNE, K-means), but the authors hypothesize that these representations may exhibit hierarchical organizational structures, which remain unexplored. Understanding such hierarchical patterns could provide deeper insight into how neural networks internally organize and represent knowledge.
AI.method: Two hierarchical clustering algorithms (Single-Linkage Clustering/SLINK and HDBSCAN) are applied to representations from a speaker recognition network to detect hierarchical clusters. A novel Hierarchical Cluster-Class Matching (HCCM) algorithm performs one-to-one matching between semantic classes and clusters. A new metric, Liebig's score, is introduced to quantify matching performance and diagnose limiting factors.
AI.result: Hierarchical clustering phenomena exist in the network representation space. Some hierarchical clusters match individual semantic classes (e.g., male, UK), while others match conjunctions of classes (e.g., male AND UK, female AND Ireland). Liebig's score successfully diagnoses the factor most strongly limiting matching performance.
AI.conclusion: The paper demonstrates that speaker recognition network representations exhibit hierarchical rather than merely flat organizational patterns, and provides tools (HCCM, Liebig's score) to analyze and quantify these structures, advancing XAI methods for understanding neural network representations.

title: Audio2Tool: Bridging Spoken Language Understanding and Function Calling
summary: Voice assistants increasingly rely on Speech Language Models (SpeechLMs) to interpret spoken queries and execute complex tasks, yet existing benchmarks lack domain breadth, acoustic diversity, and compositional reasoning complexity to evaluate tool-calling performance. We introduce Audio2Tool, a large-scale dataset comprising approximately 30,000 queries designed to assess tool-calling capabilities of SpeechLMs across three primary domains: Smart Car, Smart Home, and Wearables. Our benchmark features a multi-tier complexity hierarchy, ranging from simple direct commands to complex multi-intent and needle-in-a-haystack extraction to isolate distinct failure modes. To ensure realism, we employ zero-shot voice cloning text-to-speech synthesis and diverse noise profiles to simulate in-the-wild conditions. Evaluations of state-of-the-art SpeechLMs and ASR-LLM pipelines show strong performance on simple commands but significant degradation under compositional and acoustic challenges. We will release the dataset and benchmark upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: Audio2Tool is a large-scale dataset (~30,000 queries) for evaluating tool-calling abilities of Speech Language Models across Smart Car, Smart Home, and Wearables domains, featuring multi-tier complexity from simple commands to complex multi-intent tasks, realistic voice cloning TTS, and noise augmentation.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks lack domain breadth, acoustic diversity, and compositional reasoning complexity to properly evaluate tool-calling performance of Speech Language Models.
AI.method: Constructed a ~30k query dataset across three domains (Smart Car, Smart Home, Wearables) with multi-tier complexity hierarchy (simple commands, multi-intent, needle-in-a-haystack extraction), using zero-shot voice cloning TTS and diverse noise profiles for realism.
AI.result: State-of-the-art SpeechLMs and ASR-LLM pipelines perform well on simple commands but show significant degradation under compositional and acoustic challenges.
AI.conclusion: Audio2Tool reveals critical gaps in current SpeechLMs for complex tool-calling tasks, providing a benchmark to drive future improvements in robustness and compositional reasoning.

title: Accelerating Reinforcement Learning for Wind Farm Control via Expert Demonstrations
comment: Submitted to Journal of Physics: Conference Series (Torque 2026). This is the Accepted Manuscript version of an article accepted for publication in Journal of Physics: Conference Series. IOP Publishing Ltd is not responsible for any errors or omissions in this version of the manuscript or any version derived from it. This Accepted Manuscript is published under a CC BY licence
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) offers a promising approach for adaptive wind farm flow control, yet its practical deployment is hindered by slow training convergence and poor initial performance, factors that could translate to years of reduced power output if an untrained agent were deployed directly. This work investigates whether domain knowledge from steady-state wake models can accelerate RL training and improve initial controller performance. We propose a pretraining methodology in which expert demonstrations are generated by deploying a PyWake-based steady-state optimizer within a dynamic wake simulation (WindGym), then used to initialize both the actor and critic networks of a Soft Actor-Critic agent via behavior cloning. Experiments on a 2x2 wind farm show that pretraining eliminates the costly initial learning phase: while an untrained agent underperforms the greedy zero-yaw baseline by approximately 12%, pretraining raises initial performance to near-baseline levels. During online fine-tuning, all configurations converge within 250,000 environment steps to achieve similar performance, ultimately exceeding that of a lookup-table controller, which reaches approximately 7% power gain after 500,000 steps.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a pretraining method using steady-state wake model demonstrations to accelerate RL training for wind farm flow control, eliminating the initial poor performance phase and matching/exceeding baseline controllers.
AI.motivation: RL-based adaptive wind farm flow control suffers from slow training convergence and poor initial performance, which could cause years of reduced power output if deployed untrained.
AI.method: Expert demonstrations are generated by deploying a PyWake-based steady-state optimizer within a dynamic wake simulation (WindGym), then used to initialize both actor and critic networks of a Soft Actor-Critic agent via behavior cloning.
AI.result: Pretraining raises initial performance to near-baseline levels (vs. ~12% underperformance for untrained agent). All configurations converge within 250,000 steps, ultimately exceeding lookup-table controller (~7% power gain after 500,000 steps).
AI.conclusion: Domain knowledge from steady-state wake models can effectively accelerate RL training and improve initial controller performance for wind farm flow control.

title: Speech Enhancement Based on Drifting Models
comment: 6 pages, 2 figures
summary: We propose Speech Enhancement based on Drifting Models (DriftSE), a novel generative framework that formulates denoising as an equilibrium problem. Rather than relying on iterative sampling, DriftSE natively achieves one-step inference by evolving the pushforward distribution of a mapping function to directly match the clean speech distribution. This evolution is driven by a Drifting Field, a learned correction vector that guides samples toward the high-density regions of the clean distribution, which naturally facilitates training on unpaired data by matching distributions rather than paired samples. We investigate the framework under two formulations: a direct mapping from the noisy observation, and a stochastic conditional generative model from a Gaussian prior. Experiments on the VoiceBank-DEMAND benchmark demonstrate that DriftSE achieves high-fidelity enhancement in a single step, outperforming multi-step diffusion baselines and establishing a new paradigm for speech enhancement.

AI.tldr: DriftSE proposes a generative speech enhancement framework that achieves one-step denoising by learning a Drifting Field to pushforward noisy distributions toward clean speech distributions, outperforming multi-step diffusion models.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based speech enhancement methods require iterative sampling steps, which is computationally expensive. The authors aim to achieve high-quality one-step inference without sacrificing fidelity.
AI.method: DriftSE formulates denoising as an equilibrium problem by evolving the pushforward distribution of a mapping function via a Drifting Field—a learned correction vector that guides samples toward high-density regions of the clean speech distribution. Two formulations are explored: direct mapping from noisy observation and stochastic conditional generative model from Gaussian prior. The framework supports training on unpaired data.
AI.result: Experiments on VoiceBank-DEMAND benchmark show DriftSE achieves high-fidelity enhancement in a single step, outperforming multi-step diffusion baselines.
AI.conclusion: DriftSE establishes a new paradigm for speech enhancement by enabling one-step generative enhancement that surpasses traditional iterative diffusion approaches.

title: Spectro-Temporal Modulation Representation Framework for Human-Imitated Speech Detection
summary: Human-imitated speech poses a greater challenge than AI-generated speech for both human listeners and automatic detection systems. Unlike AI-generated speech, which often contains artifacts, over-smoothed spectra, or robotic cues, imitated speech is produced naturally by humans, thereby preserving a higher degree of naturalness that makes imitation-based speech forgery significantly more challenging to detect using conventional acoustic or cepstral features. To overcome this challenge, this study proposes an auditory perception-based Spectro-Temporal Modulation (STM) representation framework for human-imitated speech detection. The STM representations are derived from two cochlear filterbank models: the Gammatone Filterbank (GTFB), which simulates frequency selectivity and can be regarded as a first approximation of cochlear filtering, and the Gammachirp Filterbank (GCFB), which further models both frequency selectivity and level-dependent asymmetry. These STM representations jointly capture temporal and spectral fluctuations in speech signals, corresponding to changes over time in the spectrogram and variations along the frequency axis related to human auditory perception. We also introduce a Segmental-STM representation to analyze short-term modulation patterns across overlapping time windows, enabling high-resolution modeling of temporal speech variations. Experimental results show that STM representations are effective for human-imitated speech detection, achieving accuracy levels close to those of human listeners. In addition, Segmental-STM representations are more effective, surpassing human perceptual performance. The findings demonstrate that perceptually inspired spectro-temporal modeling is promising for detecting imitation-based speech attacks and improving voice authentication robustness.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an auditory perception-based Spectro-Temporal Modulation (STM) framework using Gammatone and Gammachirp filterbanks to detect human-imitated speech, achieving near-human accuracy with STM and surpassing human performance with Segmental-STM representations.
AI.motivation: Human-imitated speech is more difficult to detect than AI-generated speech because it lacks the acoustic artifacts, over-smoothed spectra, or robotic cues typical of synthetic speech, preserving high naturalness. Conventional acoustic or cepstral features fail to reliably distinguish imitated speech from genuine speech.
AI.method: The authors propose an auditory perception-based Spectro-Temporal Modulation (STM) framework derived from two cochlear filterbank models: Gammatone Filterbank (GTFB) for frequency selectivity, and Gammachirp Filterbank (GCFB) for both frequency selectivity and level-dependent asymmetry. A Segmental-STM variant is introduced to analyze short-term modulation patterns across overlapping time windows for high-resolution temporal modeling.
AI.result: STM representations achieved accuracy levels close to those of human listeners for human-imitated speech detection. Segmental-STM representations were more effective, surpassing human perceptual performance.
AI.conclusion: Perceptually inspired spectro-temporal modeling is a promising approach for detecting imitation-based speech attacks and improving voice authentication robustness.

title: Load constrained wind farm flow control through multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning
comment: Submitted to Journal of Physics: Conference Series (Torque 2026). This is the Accepted Manuscript version of an article accepted for publication in Journal of Physics: Conference Series. IOP Publishing Ltd is not responsible for any errors or omissions in this version of the manuscript or any version derived from it. This Accepted Manuscript is published under a CC BY licence
summary: This study presents a multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for load-constrained wind farm flow control (WFFC). While wake steering can enhance total wind farm power, it often introduces increased structural loads on downstream turbines. To address this, we integrate an Independent Soft Actor-Critic (I-SAC) architecture with a data-driven, local inflow sector-averaged surrogate model to provide real-time estimates of Damage Equivalent Loads (DELs). By incorporating these estimates into a shaped reward function, turbine-specific agents are trained to maximize power production while adhering to specific load-increase thresholds ($Δ_{max}$) of 10%, 20%, and 30% relative to a baseline controller. The framework is implemented within the WindGym environment using the DYNAMIKS flow solver with Dynamic Wake Meandering (DWM) model to capture non-stationary wake physics. Results indicate that the MARL agents successfully learn collaborative policies that prioritise power gain while actively retreating from high-DEL control strategies.

AI.tldr: A multi-agent RL framework (I-SAC) with a load surrogate model enables wind farm agents to maximize power while respecting structural load constraints (10-30% DEL thresholds) in the WindGym/DYNAMIKS environment.
AI.motivation: Wake steering increases total wind farm power but introduces increased structural loads on downstream turbines; existing methods lack real-time load-constrained control.
AI.method: Integrates Independent Soft Actor-Critic (I-SAC) with a data-driven local inflow sector-averaged surrogate model for real-time DEL estimation; shaped reward function enforces load-increase thresholds ($\Delta_{max}$ of 10%, 20%, 30%); implemented in WindGym with DYNAMIKS/DWM solver.
AI.result: MARL agents learned collaborative policies that prioritize power gain while actively retreating from high-DEL control strategies, successfully adhering to specified load constraints.
AI.conclusion: The MARL framework effectively balances power maximization and structural load constraints in wind farm flow control, demonstrating feasibility of real-time load-aware cooperative control.

title: An event-based sequence modeling approach to recognizing non-triad chords with oversegmentation minimization
comment: accepted to ICASSP 2026
summary: Automatic chord recognition (ACR) extracts time-aligned chord labels from music audio recordings. Despite recent advances, ACR still struggles with oversegmentation, data scarcity, and imbalance, especially in recognizing complex chords such as non-triads, which are unpopular in existing datasets. To address these challenges, we reformulate ACR as a segment-level sequence-to-sequence prediction task, where chord sequences are predicted auto-regressively rather than frame by frame. This design mitigates excessive segmentation by detecting chord changes only at segment boundaries. We further introduce two types of token representations and an encoder pre-training method, both specifically designed for time-aligned chord modeling. Experimental results show that our model improves performance in both chord recognition and segmentation, with notable gains for complex and infrequent chord types. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of segment-level sequence modeling, structured tokenization, and representation learning for advancing chord recognition systems.

AI.tldr: This paper reformulates automatic chord recognition (ACR) as a segment-level sequence-to-sequence prediction task using auto-regressive chord sequence prediction, with specialized token representations and encoder pre-training, achieving improvements in chord recognition and segmentation, particularly for complex and infrequent chord types.
AI.motivation: ACR suffers from oversegmentation, data scarcity, and class imbalance, particularly for complex chords (non-triads) that are underrepresented in existing datasets.
AI.method: Reformulates ACR as segment-level sequence-to-sequence prediction where chord sequences are predicted auto-regressively at segment boundaries rather than frame-by-frame; introduces two types of token representations and an encoder pre-training method designed for time-aligned chord modeling.
AI.result: The model improves performance in both chord recognition and segmentation, with notable gains for complex and infrequent chord types.
AI.conclusion: Segment-level sequence modeling, structured tokenization, and representation learning are effective for advancing chord recognition systems.

title: Opening the Design Space: Two Years of Performance with Intelligent Musical Instruments
comment: Accepted for publication at the International Conference on New Interfaces for Musical Expression (NIME) 2026
summary: Machine generation of symbolic music and digital audio are hot topics but there have been relatively few digital musical instruments that integrate generative AI. Present musical AI tools are not artist centred and do not support experimentation or integrating into musical instruments or practices. This work introduces an inexpensive generative AI instrument platform based on a single board computer that connects via MIDI to other musical devices. The platform uses artist-collected datasets with models trained on a regular computer. This paper asks what the design space of intelligent musical instruments might look like when accessible and portable AI systems are available for artistic exploration. I contribute five examples of instruments created and tested through a two-year first-person artistic research process. These show that (re)mapping can replace retraining for discovering AI interaction, that fast input interleaving is a new co-creative strategy, that small-data AI models can be a transportable design resource, and that cheap hardware can lower barriers to inclusion. This work could enable artists to explore new interaction and performance schemes with intelligent musical instruments.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces an inexpensive generative AI instrument platform using a single-board computer and MIDI connectivity, with artist-collected datasets and small-data models. Through a two-year first-person artistic research, the author presents five instruments demonstrating that (re)mapping can replace retraining, fast input interleaving is a new co-creative strategy, small-data AI models are transportable design resources, and cheap hardware lowers barriers to inclusion.
AI.motivation: Current generative AI music tools are not artist-centered, lack support for experimentation, and are not easily integrated into musical instruments or practices. There is a need for accessible, portable AI systems that enable artistic exploration in intelligent musical instruments.
AI.method: The author developed an inexpensive generative AI instrument platform based on a single-board computer with MIDI connectivity, using artist-collected datasets with models trained on a regular computer. A two-year first-person artistic research process was conducted, creating and testing five example instruments.
AI.result: (Re)mapping can replace retraining for discovering AI interaction; fast input interleaving is a new co-creative strategy; small-data AI models can be transportable design resources; cheap hardware can lower barriers to inclusion.
AI.conclusion: This work could enable artists to explore new interaction and performance schemes with intelligent musical instruments, expanding the design space of accessible and portable AI systems for artistic exploration.

title: Hierarchical RL-MPC Control for Dynamic Wake Steering in Wind Farms
comment: This work has been submitted to IFAC for possible publication
summary: Wind farm wake steering optimization is challenging due to complex flow physics and changing conditions. This paper presents a hierarchical framework that combines reinforcement learning with model predictive control, where an RL agent learns compensatory state estimates for an MPC controller, rather than directly controlling turbines. Evaluated on a three-turbine case, the approach achieves a 23\% power gain over the baseline control and surpasses the idealized MPC with perfect state knowledge. Compared to direct RL control, the hybrid architecture maintains superior safety characteristics during training while achieving comparable performance with more stable control actions.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical framework combining reinforcement learning and model predictive control for wind farm wake steering, where RL compensates state estimates for MPC, achieving 23% power gain and better safety than direct RL control.
AI.motivation: Wind farm wake steering optimization is challenging due to complex flow physics and changing conditions, motivating a need for advanced control approaches.
AI.method: A hierarchical framework combining reinforcement learning with model predictive control, where an RL agent learns compensatory state estimates for an MPC controller rather than directly controlling turbines.
AI.result: Achieves 23% power gain over baseline control, surpasses idealized MPC with perfect state knowledge, and maintains superior safety characteristics during training compared to direct RL control.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid RL-MPC architecture offers comparable performance to direct RL control but with more stable control actions and better safety characteristics during training.

title: All That Glitters Is Not Audio: Rethinking Text Priors and Audio Reliance in Audio-Language Evaluation
comment: 6 pages, 3 figures, 5 tables
summary: Large Audio-Language Models show consistent performance gains across speech and audio benchmarks, yet high scores may not reflect true auditory perception. If a model can answer questions without processing the acoustic signal, the benchmark fails as a measure of auditory understanding. We present a diagnostic framework using two axes: text prior, which measures answerability from text and general knowledge alone, and audio reliance, which assesses actual dependency on the acoustic signal. Evaluating eight LALMs across three benchmarks, we find that models retain 60-72% of their full audio scores even without any audio input. Moreover, among items that require audio, only 3.0-4.2% need the complete audio clip; the majority can be resolved using localized fragments. These findings challenge the assumption that benchmark performance equals robust audio understanding, and we conclude with practical guidelines for improving evaluation reliability and benchmark design.

AI.tldr: Large Audio-Language Models achieve high benchmark scores but often do not rely on acoustic signals; they retain 60-72% accuracy without audio, and only 3-4.2% of items require the full audio clip, questioning the validity of current auditory understanding evaluations.
AI.motivation: Current benchmarks may overestimate LALMs' true auditory perception because models can answer questions without processing the acoustic signal, so a diagnostic framework is needed to measure genuine audio reliance.
AI.method: Proposes a two-axis diagnostic framework: (1) text prior — measuring answerability from text/general knowledge alone, and (2) audio reliance — assessing dependency on the acoustic signal. Evaluates eight LALMs across three benchmarks.
AI.result: Models retain 60-72% of full audio scores without audio input; only 3.0-4.2% of items require the complete audio clip; most audio-requiring items can be solved with localized fragments.
AI.conclusion: Benchmark performance does not equal robust audio understanding; provides practical guidelines for improving evaluation reliability and benchmark design.

title: HeadRouter: Dynamic Head-Weight Routing for Task-Adaptive Audio Token Pruning in Large Audio Language Models
comment: Homepage: https://dabdans.github.io/HeadRouter/
summary: Recent large audio language models (LALMs) demonstrate remarkable capabilities in processing extended multi-modal sequences, yet incur high inference costs. Token compression is an effective method that directly reduces redundant tokens in the sequence. Existing compression methods usually assume that all attention heads in LALMs contribute equally to various audio tasks and calculate token importance by averaging scores across all heads. However, our analysis demonstrates that attention heads exhibit distinct behaviors across diverse audio domains. We further reveal that only a sparse subset of attention heads actively responds to audio, with completely different performance when handling semantic and acoustic tasks. In light of this observation, we propose HeadRouter, a head-importance-aware token pruning method that perceives the varying importance of attention heads in different audio tasks to maximize the retention of crucial tokens. HeadRouter is training-free and can be applied to various LALMs. Extensive experiments on the AudioMarathon and MMAU-Pro benchmarks demonstrate that HeadRouter achieves state-of-the-art compression performance, exceeding the baseline model even when retaining 70% of the audio tokens and achieving 101.8% and 103.0% of the vanilla average on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, respectively.

AI.tldr: HeadRouter is a training-free token pruning method for large audio language models that perceives varying importance of attention heads across different audio tasks, achieving state-of-the-art compression (101.8% and 103.0% of vanilla performance on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B/7B when retaining 70% audio tokens).
AI.motivation: Existing token compression methods assume all attention heads contribute equally across audio tasks and compute token importance via averaging scores across all heads, but this overlooks the distinct behaviors and sparse activation patterns of attention heads in different audio domains (semantic vs. acoustic tasks).
AI.method: HeadRouter is a head-importance-aware token pruning method that perceives varying importance of attention heads for different audio tasks to maximize retention of crucial tokens. It is training-free and applicable to various LALMs.
AI.result: HeadRouter achieves state-of-the-art compression on AudioMarathon and MMAU-Pro benchmarks, exceeding the baseline when retaining 70% audio tokens, achieving 101.8% and 103.0% of vanilla average on Qwen2.5-Omni-3B and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B respectively.
AI.conclusion: HeadRouter effectively addresses the limitations of uniform head importance assumption in token compression by leveraging head-specific importance for different audio tasks, yielding better compression without training.

title: Integrated Lander-Propulsion-GNC Framework for Autonomous Lunar Powered Descent
comment: Accepted at IEEE RAST 2026, 13-15 May, Istanbul, Türkiye. 6 pages. \c{opyright} 2026 IEEE. Personal use permitted; other uses require IEEE permission
summary: This paper presents an integrated lander-propulsion-GNC framework for autonomous lunar powered descent. The BUG VTVL test vehicle serves as the reference platform, with the YUNT V0 throttleable bipropellant engine providing variable thrust across a wide operating envelope, integrated with a real-time successive convexification guidance solver. The vehicle design accounts for structural configuration, landing stability, center-of-mass migration, and inertia evolution, while the propulsion architecture defines the throttle ratio, dead-zone behavior, and gimbal authority that constrain the guidance problem. A successive convexification algorithm addresses all nonconvexities; thrust lower bounds, mass depletion coupling, and thruster dead-zone behavior are all handled within a unified second-order cone program solvable in near-real time. Parametric analysis reveals a fundamental coupling between throttle ratio, pointing authority, and surface gravity. Monte Carlo simulations validate guidance robustness, achieving sub-50-meter landing precision under realistic perturbations.

AI.tldr: An integrated lander-propulsion-GNC framework for autonomous lunar powered descent is presented, using the BUG VTVL vehicle and YUNT V0 engine, with a real-time successive convexification guidance solver achieving sub-50-meter landing precision under realistic perturbations.
AI.motivation: To develop an autonomous lunar powered descent framework that integrates lander structural design, propulsion constraints, and guidance navigation control (GNC) to address the tight coupling between vehicle configuration, engine characteristics, and real-time trajectory optimization.
AI.method: The framework integrates the BUG VTVL test vehicle with the YUNT V0 throttleable bipropellant engine. A successive convexification algorithm solves all nonconvexities (thrust lower bounds, mass depletion coupling, thruster dead-zone behavior) within a unified second-order cone program solvable in near-real time. Parametric analysis and Monte Carlo simulations are employed.
AI.result: Parametric analysis reveals fundamental coupling between throttle ratio, pointing authority, and surface gravity. Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate sub-50-meter landing precision under realistic perturbations, validating guidance robustness.
AI.conclusion: The integrated lander-propulsion-GNC framework successfully handles propulsion and structural constraints in real-time, achieving high landing precision for autonomous lunar descent.

title: RTCFake: Speech Deepfake Detection in Real-Time Communication
comment: Accepted by ACL 2026
summary: With the rapid advancement of speech generation technologies, the threat posed by speech deepfakes in real-time communication (RTC) scenarios has intensified. However, existing detection studies mainly focus on offline simulations and struggle to cope with the complex distortions introduced during RTC transmission, including unknown speech enhancement processes (e.g., noise suppression) and codec compression. To address this challenge, we present the first large-scale speech deepfake dataset tailored for RTC scenarios, termed \textit{RTCFake}, totaling approximately 600 hours. The dataset is constructed by transmitting speech through multiple mainstream social media and conferencing platforms (e.g., Zoom), enabling precise pairing between offline and online speech. In addition, we propose a phoneme-guided consistency learning (PCL) strategy that enforces models to learn platform-invariant semantic structural representations. In this paper, the RTCFake dataset is divided into training, development, and evaluation sets. The evaluation set further includes both unseen RTC platforms and unseen complex noise conditions, thereby providing a more realistic and challenging evaluation benchmark for speech deepfake detection. Furthermore, the proposed PCL strategy achieves significant improvements in both cross-platform generalization and noise robustness, offering an effective and generalizable modeling paradigm. The \textit{RTCFake} dataset is provided in the {https://huggingface.co/datasets/JunXueTech/RTCFake}.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces RTCFake, the first large-scale (~600 hours) speech deepfake dataset for real-time communication (RTC) scenarios, constructed by transmitting speech through platforms like Zoom. It also proposes a phoneme-guided consistency learning (PCL) strategy to improve cross-platform generalization and noise robustness in deepfake detection.
AI.motivation: Existing speech deepfake detection studies focus on offline simulations and cannot handle complex distortions (noise suppression, codec compression) introduced during real-time communication transmission. There is a lack of large-scale RTC-specific datasets and robust detection methods.
AI.method: The authors construct RTCFake (~600 hours) by transmitting speech through multiple mainstream social media and conferencing platforms, enabling precise offline-online pairing. They propose a phoneme-guided consistency learning (PCL) strategy that learns platform-invariant semantic structural representations.
AI.result: The evaluation set includes unseen RTC platforms and complex noise conditions, providing a realistic benchmark. PCL achieves significant improvements in cross-platform generalization and noise robustness.
AI.conclusion: RTCFake addresses the gap in RTC-specific deepfake detection datasets, and PCL offers an effective, generalizable modeling paradigm for real-world speech deepfake detection.

title: Probabilistic Hazard Analysis Framework with Stochastic Optimal Control for Deteriorating Civil Infrastructure Systems
summary: The safety and resilience of civil infrastructure systems are increasingly threatened by compounded risks from various hazard events and structural deterioration due to environmental stressors. This study presents a comprehensive risk-informed, life-cycle optimization framework that extends the Performance-Based Earthquake Engineering (PBEE) and probabilistic seismic loss estimation paradigms by combining hazard uncertainties, nonstationary deterioration, structural damage accumulation, and state-dependent fragility assessments, with optimal, adaptive maintenance strategies in time. The life-cycle cost optimization is formulated in this work as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) problem, utilizing derived, transition matrices reflecting time-variant deterioration effects and hazard risks. To mitigate the curse of dimensionality in system-level optimization, a novel tensor-based method exploiting Kronecker-factored transition dynamics is introduced, reducing complexity from exponential to linear in the number of components while still preserving exact, global dynamic programming solutions. Overall, the framework is general and versatile, able to accommodate various hazard types. A seismic hazard application is, however, demonstrated and explained in detail in this work. The developed methodology eventually provides decision-makers with a practical, data-driven tool toward cost effective risk mitigation of civil infrastructure systems.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a risk-informed, life-cycle optimization framework for civil infrastructure that integrates hazard uncertainties, structural deterioration, damage accumulation, and adaptive maintenance strategies via a Markov Decision Process, with a novel tensor-based method using Kronecker-factored transition dynamics to reduce computational complexity from exponential to linear in the number of components, demonstrated through a seismic hazard application.
AI.motivation: The safety and resilience of civil infrastructure systems are increasingly threatened by compounded risks from various hazard events and structural deterioration due to environmental stressors, necessitating a more comprehensive risk management framework.
AI.method: The study extends PBEE and probabilistic seismic loss estimation by combining hazard uncertainties, nonstationary deterioration, structural damage accumulation, state-dependent fragility assessments, and adaptive maintenance strategies. The life-cycle cost optimization is formulated as a Markov Decision Process with time-variant transition matrices. A tensor-based method exploiting Kronecker-factored transition dynamics reduces complexity from exponential to linear in components while preserving exact global dynamic programming solutions.
AI.result: The framework successfully reduces computational complexity from exponential to linear in the number of components via the Kronecker-factored tensor method, enabling exact global dynamic programming solutions for system-level optimization.
AI.conclusion: The framework provides decision-makers with a practical, data-driven tool for cost-effective risk mitigation of civil infrastructure systems, demonstrated through a seismic hazard application.

title: Learning the Weather-Grid Nexus via Weather-to-Voltage (W2V) Predictive Modeling
comment: 10 pages, 10 figures, Submitted to IEEE Transactions on Sustainable Energy
summary: This paper proposes a weather-to-voltage (W2V) predictive modeling framework to learn the underlying weather-grid nexus. Unlike existing approaches on weather-informed grid operations, our proposed W2V model can achieve the joint analysis of weather and grid states, and further leverage this coupling to enhance grid-aware weather forecasting (GAWF) as a key application. To achieve this end-to-end learning, the W2V model acts as a differentiable surrogate for weather-incorporated power flow analysis by mapping weather features at high spatial resolution directly to grid-wide bus voltages. Thanks to a compact neural network design and principal component analysis based initialization, it achieves high voltage prediction accuracy and numerical stability during training. Building on this capability, W2V-based voltage signals are used to guide the development of GAWF that can account for its downstream voltage prediction performance. Using a 6717-bus Texas synthetic test system with meteorological inputs from 701 weather locations, our numerical tests have verified the excellent accuracy and generalizability of the proposed W2V model. More importantly, the W2V model has enabled the GAWF to effectively prioritize the weather features and conditions that are most critical to grid operations, such as system-wide quick wind drops preceding ramp-ups.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a Weather-to-Voltage (W2V) framework that learns the weather-grid nexus using a differentiable surrogate for power flow analysis, enabling grid-aware weather forecasting (GAWF) that identifies critical weather features for grid operations.
AI.motivation: Existing approaches on weather-informed grid operations cannot achieve joint analysis of weather and grid states, nor leverage this coupling to enhance weather forecasting with grid awareness.
AI.method: The W2V model is a compact neural network with PCA-based initialization that acts as a differentiable surrogate for weather-incorporated power flow analysis, mapping high-resolution weather features directly to bus voltages. It enables Grid-Aware Weather Forecasting (GAWF) by using W2V-based voltage signals to guide weather forecasting toward downstream voltage prediction performance.
AI.result: Tested on a 6717-bus Texas synthetic system with 701 weather locations, the W2V model achieves high voltage prediction accuracy, numerical stability, and generalizability. GAWF effectively prioritizes critical weather features such as system-wide quick wind drops preceding ramp-ups.
AI.conclusion: The W2V framework successfully bridges weather and grid states in an end-to-end differentiable manner, enabling grid-aware weather forecasting that focuses on operationally critical weather conditions.

title: RAS: a Reliability Oriented Metric for Automatic Speech Recognition
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures
summary: Automatic speech recognition systems often produce confident yet incorrect transcriptions under noisy or ambiguous conditions, which can be misleading for both users and downstream applications. Standard evaluation based on Word Error Rate focuses solely on accuracy and fails to capture transcription reliability. We introduce an abstention-aware transcription framework that enables ASR models to explicitly abstain from uncertain segments. To evaluate reliability under abstention, we propose RAS, a reliability-oriented metric that balances transcription informativeness and error aversion, with its trade-off parameter calibrated by human preference. We then train an abstention-aware ASR model through supervised bootstrapping followed by reinforcement learning. Our experiments demonstrate substantial improvements in transcription reliability while maintaining competitive accuracy.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an abstention-aware ASR framework that allows models to abstain from uncertain speech segments, introduces a RAS metric to evaluate transcription reliability, and uses supervised bootstrapping plus reinforcement learning to improve reliability while maintaining accuracy.
AI.motivation: Standard ASR systems produce confident but incorrect transcriptions under noisy conditions, and existing metrics like Word Error Rate fail to capture transcription reliability, which can mislead users and downstream applications.
AI.method: 1) An abstention-aware transcription framework enabling models to abstain from uncertain segments; 2) RAS (Reliability-oriented metric) that balances informativeness and error aversion with human-calibrated trade-off; 3) Training via supervised bootstrapping followed by reinforcement learning.
AI.result: Substantial improvements in transcription reliability while maintaining competitive accuracy compared to standard ASR systems.
AI.conclusion: Abstention-aware ASR with reliability-oriented evaluation (RAS) effectively addresses overconfident erroneous transcriptions, offering a practical path toward more trustworthy automatic speech recognition.

title: System-Level Impacts of Flexible Data Center Load Scheduling on Cost, Emissions, and Transmission Congestion
summary: Large data centers are being deployed in the U.S. at an unprecedented rate, introducing significant flexible load potential. A portion of data center workloads - best-effort (BE) jobs - can be scheduled flexibly to reduce power system operating costs and emissions. However, the system-level impacts of such scheduling remain underexplored. This paper investigates the effects of flexible data center load scheduling on operating cost, system stress, and emissions using the ACTIVSg2000 2000-bus test system. Results show that BE loads shift toward periods of lower locational marginal prices (LMPs), typically aligned with high renewable generation. Importantly, latency-critical (LC) workloads remain unaffected, preserving quality of service (QoS). Flexible scheduling also leads to reductions in both greenhouse gas and toxic emissions, as well as transmission congestion, compared to inflexible operation, demonstrating its potential to support more efficient and sustainable grid operation.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes how flexible scheduling of best-effort data center workloads can reduce power system operating costs, emissions, and transmission congestion by shifting loads to periods with lower locational marginal prices and higher renewable generation, without affecting latency-critical workloads or quality of service.
AI.motivation: Large data centers are rapidly expanding in the U.S., creating significant flexible load potential. However, the system-level impacts of scheduling best-effort workloads flexibly on power system operating cost, stress, and emissions remain underexplored.
AI.method: The study uses the ACTIVSg2000 2000-bus test system to simulate and evaluate the effects of flexible data center load scheduling on operating cost, system stress, and emissions.
AI.result: BE loads shift toward periods of lower LMPs aligned with high renewable generation. LC workloads and QoS remain unaffected. Flexible scheduling reduces greenhouse gas and toxic emissions and transmission congestion compared to inflexible operation.
AI.conclusion: Flexible scheduling of best-effort data center workloads demonstrates potential to support more efficient and sustainable grid operation.

title: An Algebraic State Observer for a Class of Physical Systems
summary: In this paper we present a radically new approach to design state observers for nonlinear systems, with particular emphasis on physical ones. Our objective is to obtain an algebraic relation between the unmeasurable part of the state and filtered versions of the systems inputs and outputs, which holds true for all $t \geq 0$. The latter qualifier should be contrasted with the usual asymptotic (or fixed/finite time) objective. The standing assumption for our design is the availability -- or possibility of constructing, via coordinate change -- state components with measurable derivatives. In the physical systems studied in the paper this condition is naturally satisfied. The next step in the design is the application of the Swapping Lemma to pull out from the dynamics the derivative of one of these signals. The design is completed replacing the latter by the measurable signals and arranging the remaining terms. The algebraic observer constitutes a refreshing major departure from classical asymptotic observer designs, even in the case of electrical motors and mechanical systems that have been exhaustively studied. Particularly notable is the fact that no observability or excitation condition is imposed for the construction of the algebraic observer.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a new approach for designing algebraic observers for nonlinear physical systems. The key idea is to exploit state components with measurable derivatives and use the Swapping Lemma to derive an algebraic relation between unmeasurable states and filtered inputs/outputs that holds for all time, rather than asymptotically. No observability or excitation conditions are required.
AI.motivation: To overcome limitations of classical asymptotic observer designs by developing an algebraic (finite-time, non-asymptotic) observer that requires no observability or excitation conditions, suitable for physical systems with measurable state derivatives.
AI.method: The approach relies on: (1) availability of state components with measurable derivatives (naturally satisfied in physical systems); (2) applying the Swapping Lemma to extract derivatives from the dynamics; (3) replacing derivatives with measurable signals to obtain algebraic relations between unmeasurable states and filtered inputs/outputs.
AI.result: An algebraic observer valid for all t ≥ 0 is obtained, requiring no observability or excitation conditions. The method is demonstrated on electrical motors and mechanical systems.
AI.conclusion: The algebraic observer represents a major departure from classical asymptotic observer designs, offering a refreshing alternative that avoids asymptotic convergence requirements and restrictive assumptions like persistence of excitation.

title: GPU-Native Multi-Area State Estimation via SIMD Abstraction and Boundary Condensation
summary: Power system state estimation (SE) is foundational for grid monitoring, yet conventional centralized solvers face increasing computational pressure as the system scale and real-time requirements grow. This paper presents a GPU-native framework for hierarchical multi-area state estimation (MASE) that addresses these bottlenecks through a single-instruction, multiple-data (SIMD) abstraction and sparse Schur local condensation. We partition the network into areas, evaluate measurement residuals and derivatives using fixed-sparsity templates, and directly assemble local normal-equation blocks through a fused GPU accumulation kernel without materializing explicit Jacobians. Each area is then factorized on the GPU in Schur mode to export a dense local boundary block and condensed right-hand side, after which a reduced global boundary system is assembled and solved on device. This design preserves device residency across measurement evaluation, local condensation, and boundary coordination while exposing parallelism across areas. Numerical experiments on partitioned PEGASE 2869-bus, PEGASE 9241-bus, and ACTIVSg10k benchmark systems demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively leverages GPU throughput by maintaining full device residency and high arithmetic intensity.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a GPU-native hierarchical multi-area state estimation framework that uses SIMD abstraction and sparse Schur local condensation to improve computational efficiency. The method keeps all processing on the GPU (measurement evaluation, local factorization, boundary coordination) and demonstrates effectiveness on large benchmark systems up to 10k buses.
AI.motivation: Conventional centralized solvers for power system state estimation face increasing computational pressure as system scale and real-time requirements grow.
AI.method: The method partitions the network into areas, uses fixed-sparsity templates for measurement residuals and derivatives, assembles local normal-equation blocks via fused GPU accumulation kernels (avoiding explicit Jacobians), factorizes each area on GPU in Schur mode, assembles and solves a reduced global boundary system on device, maintaining full device residency throughout.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on PEGASE 2869-bus, PEGASE 9241-bus, and ACTIVSg10k benchmark systems show the approach effectively leverages GPU throughput with full device residency and high arithmetic intensity.
AI.conclusion: The GPU-native hierarchical MASE framework with SIMD abstraction and sparse Schur local condensation successfully addresses computational bottlenecks in large-scale power system state estimation by keeping all operations device-resident.

title: An Exponentially stable Extended Kalman Filter with Estimate dependent Process noise Covariance for Chemical Reaction Networks
summary: Biomolecular systems are often modeled with partially known nonlinear stochastic dynamics, making state and parameter estimation a central challenge. While Kalman filtering techniques are widely used in this setting, their performance critically depends on the choice of the process noise covariance, which is typically assumed constant and heuristically tuned. Such assumptions are not justified for biomolecular systems, where intrinsic noise arises from underlying reaction kinetics. In this work, we propose an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) with a state estimate-dependent process noise covariance based on Chemical Langevin Equation (CLE). Further, we analyze the stochastic stability of the proposed filter and derive conditions under which the estimation error remains exponentially bounded in the mean-square sense. In particular, we obtain an upper bound on the sampling period for discrete-time biomolecular systems that guarantees this property. The proposed framework is validated through simulations on a nonlinear gene expression model. This approach enables first principle-based modeling and filter design choices for synthetic biomolecular circuits, eliminating the need for heuristic tuning of the process noise covariance.

AI.tldr: Proposes an Extended Kalman Filter with state-dependent process noise covariance based on the Chemical Langevin Equation for biomolecular systems, analyzes its stochastic stability, and derives sampling period bounds for mean-square exponential error boundedness.
AI.motivation: Biomolecular systems often have partially known nonlinear stochastic dynamics; standard Kalman filters assume constant process noise covariance tuned heuristically, which is inadequate for biomolecular systems where intrinsic noise arises from reaction kinetics.
AI.method: Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) with state estimate-dependent process noise covariance derived from the Chemical Langevin Equation (CLE); stochastic stability analysis via mean-square exponential boundedness conditions; derivation of an upper bound on the sampling period for discrete-time systems.
AI.result: Validated through simulations on a nonlinear gene expression model; the approach enables first principle-based modeling and eliminates heuristic tuning of process noise covariance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed EKF with CLE-based state-dependent noise covariance provides theoretically grounded filter design for synthetic biomolecular circuits, with proven stochastic stability under bounded sampling periods.

title: Adaptive Spatial-Temporal Graph Learning-Enabled Short-Term Voltage Stability Assessment against Time-Varying Topological Conditions
comment: 13 pages, accepted for publication in IEEE Transactions on Power Systems
summary: The emerging deep learning (DL) technology has recently exhibited great potential in data-driven short-term voltage stability (SVS) assessment of complex power grids. However, without sufficient attention to the time-varying topological structures of today's power grids, the majority of existing DL-based SVS assessment schemes could experience severe performance degradation in practice. To address this drawback, this paper proposes an adaptive spatial-temporal graph learning-enabled SVS assessment approach that can adapt well to various topological changes. First, considering the time-varying topological conditions of a given power grid, an adaptive graph representation matrix is automatically learned to effectively capture the complicated spatial correlations between individual buses within the grid. Then, to help better capture regional SVS features for subsequent learning processes, the adaptive graph representation matrix is properly adjusted by introducing a spatial attention mechanism. Further, with post-fault system trajectory data linked together via attention-based graph representation, a residual spatiotemporal graph convolutional network is carefully built with Optuna-based optimization to deeply mine system-wide spatiotemporal features and thus achieve structure-adaptive SVS assessment. Numerical test results on two representative sub-systems of a realistic provincial power grid in South China demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach under various changing topological conditions.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive spatial-temporal graph learning approach for short-term voltage stability (SVS) assessment that adapts to time-varying topological changes in power grids. It uses an adaptive graph representation matrix with spatial attention and a residual spatiotemporal graph convolutional network optimized by Optuna to capture system-wide features. Tests on a realistic provincial power grid in South China show effectiveness under changing topologies.
AI.motivation: Existing DL-based SVS assessment methods ignore time-varying topological structures of power grids, causing severe performance degradation in practice. This paper aims to address this drawback by developing a structure-adaptive approach.
AI.method: 1) An adaptive graph representation matrix is automatically learned to capture spatial correlations between buses under time-varying topologies. 2) A spatial attention mechanism adjusts the matrix to better capture regional SVS features. 3) A residual spatiotemporal graph convolutional network (with Optuna-based hyperparameter optimization) is built using post-fault trajectory data and attention-based graph representations to mine system-wide spatiotemporal features for structure-adaptive SVS assessment.
AI.result: Numerical tests on two representative sub-systems of a realistic provincial power grid in South China demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed approach under various changing topological conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed adaptive spatial-temporal graph learning approach successfully achieves structure-adaptive SVS assessment that adapts well to topological changes, overcoming the performance degradation of conventional DL-based methods.

title: sumoITScontrol: Traffic Controller Collection for SUMO Traffic Simulations
summary: Reliable benchmarking is essential for progress in intelligent traffic control research. While microscopic traffic simulators such as SUMO enable detailed modelling of individual vehicle interactions, many published control studies still rely on single-run evaluations and project-specific baseline implementations, limiting reproducibility and comparability. This paper presents sumoITScontrol, an open-source and extensible Python framework providing a curated collection of widely used traffic controllers implemented for SUMO via the TraCI interface. The framework includes established methods for both urban and freeway traffic management, such as Max Pressure signal control, SCOOT/SCATS-inspired adaptive strategies, and ramp metering algorithms including ALINEA, HERO, and METALINE. Beyond providing implementations, the paper emphasises methodological best-practices for controller evaluation in stochastic microscopic environments. Through systematic calibration and replicated simulation experiments, we demonstrate the substantial impact of stochastic variability on performance metrics and highlight the necessity of variance-aware reporting and statistical hypothesis testing. By combining standardised controller implementations with reproducibility-oriented evaluation guidelines, sumoITScontrol aims to improve methodological transparency, enable fair benchmarking of novel approaches, and strengthen experimental standards within the SUMO and intelligent transportation systems research communities. Source Code on project's GitHub page: https://github.com/DerKevinRiehl/sumoITScontrol/.

AI.tldr: sumoITScontrol is an open-source Python framework providing standardized implementations of traffic controllers (Max Pressure, SCOOT/SCATS-inspired, ALINEA, HERO, METALINE) for SUMO via TraCI, along with methodological best-practices for variance-aware evaluation including calibration, replication, and statistical hypothesis testing to improve reproducibility and benchmarking in traffic control research.
AI.motivation: Reliable benchmarking is essential for progress in intelligent traffic control, but many published studies rely on single-run evaluations and project-specific baselines, limiting reproducibility and comparability.
AI.method: The framework provides a curated collection of traffic controllers (Max Pressure, SCOOT/SCATS-inspired, ALINEA, HERO, METALINE) implemented for SUMO via TraCI. The paper emphasizes systematic calibration, replicated simulation experiments, variance-aware reporting, and statistical hypothesis testing to account for stochastic variability.
AI.result: Demonstrates the substantial impact of stochastic variability on performance metrics and highlights the necessity of variance-aware reporting and statistical hypothesis testing through systematic calibration and replicated experiments.
AI.conclusion: sumoITScontrol aims to improve methodological transparency, enable fair benchmarking of novel approaches, and strengthen experimental standards within SUMO and ITS research communities.

title: Robust Operation of Distribution Networks: Generalized Uncertainty Modelling in Confidence-Level-Based Information Gap Decision
summary: This paper studies the robust optimal operation of distribution networks (DNs) under renewable generation and load demand uncertainties, seeking an improved trade-off between robustness and economic performance. Building upon information gap decision theory (IGDT), a generalized uncertainty modelling is proposed to enhance the expressiveness of the uncertainty characterization. The proposed modelling captures both symmetric and asymmetric uncertainty features, and supports linear or nonlinear expansion of the uncertainty sets driven by confidence level. This advancement leads to the development of a confidence-level-based IGDT (CL-IGDT) framework for DN operation. To solve the resulting model, its equivalence to a family of two-stage robust optimization problems (TSROs) is established, enabling a Fibonacci search over the confidence level. To further improve computational efficiency, a cut-recycling strategy is proposed to exploit invariant information across TSROs. These techniques are integrated into a novel Fibonacci-Parametric Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm with guaranteed asymptotic convergence. Case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and demonstrate the performance advantages of the proposed algorithm.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a confidence-level-based information gap decision theory (CL-IGDT) framework for robust distribution network operation under renewable and load uncertainties, achieving improved robustness-economy trade-offs. It develops a Fibonacci-Parametric Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm with cut-recycling for efficient computation.
AI.motivation: Existing robust optimization methods for distribution network operation face limited expressiveness in uncertainty characterization and poor trade-offs between robustness and economic performance. The paper seeks to overcome these limitations by generalizing IGDT to capture both symmetric and asymmetric uncertainty features with flexible uncertainty set expansion.
AI.method: The method proposes a confidence-level-based IGDT (CL-IGDT) framework with generalized uncertainty modeling supporting symmetric/asymmetric features and linear/nonlinear expansion. The model is equivalently transformed into a family of two-stage robust optimization problems (TSROs), solved via a Fibonacci search over confidence levels. A cut-recycling strategy and Fibonacci-Parametric Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm are developed for computational efficiency.
AI.result: Case studies validate the effectiveness of the CL-IGDT framework and demonstrate performance advantages of the proposed Fibonacci-Parametric Column-and-Constraint Generation algorithm with guaranteed asymptotic convergence.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CL-IGDT framework and solution algorithm achieve an improved robustness-economy trade-off for distribution network operation under uncertainty, with efficient computation via cut-recycling and Fibonacci search techniques.

title: Private and Common Information States in Decentralized Parallel Dynamic Programming for Delayed Sharing Patterns
summary: This paper develops a dynamic programming (DP) approach for decentralized stochastic optimal control problems with delayed sharing information patterns, which exhibits the fundamental Properties of classical DP of centralized partially observable Markov decision problems (POMDPs): the value functions and information states depend on the actions of the minimizing controls and not their strategies. This is achieved by invoking the concept of Person-by-Person (PbP) optimality, in which each control strategy is associated with a value function conditioned on its assigned delayed sharing information pattern, when all other strategies are fixed to their optimal responses. The value functions satisfy generalized and simplified DP equations. These are used to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for PbP optimality. The simplified DP equations are obtained by invoking the structural property that optimal strategies are separated and functionals of two information states: 1) a private a posteriori probability distribution based on the information pattern of the strategy, and 2) a centralized a posteriori probability distribution based on the shared or common information to all strategies, each satisfying a Markov recursion. The DP approach of this paper, settles a long standing open problem since the appearance of T-step delayed sharing patterns in [1, Section IV.G], in terms of generalizing the fundamental properties of classical DP approach.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a dynamic programming approach for decentralized stochastic control with delayed sharing information patterns, using Person-by-Person optimality to derive value functions and simplified DP equations that depend on controls rather than strategies, settling a long-standing open problem.
AI.motivation: To generalize the fundamental properties of classical DP for centralized POMDPs to decentralized stochastic optimal control problems with delayed sharing information patterns, which has been an open problem since [1].
AI.method: Invokes Person-by-Person (PbP) optimality where each control strategy's value function is conditioned on its delayed sharing information pattern while others are fixed. Derives generalized and simplified DP equations. Exploits structural property that optimal strategies are separated functionals of two information states: (1) private a posteriori distribution, and (2) centralized a posteriori distribution (shared/common information), each satisfying Markov recursions.
AI.result: Value functions and information states depend on actions of minimizing controls, not their strategies. Simplified DP equations are obtained through the separation property using two information states. Necessary and sufficient conditions for PbP optimality are derived.
AI.conclusion: Settles a long-standing open problem since T-step delayed sharing patterns were introduced in [1], generalizing fundamental properties of classical DP to this setting.

title: Resource-Constrained Shortest Path with Polytopic Reset Sets
summary: This paper investigates the problem of computing the shortest path between two states under resource constraints in environments with resource-replenishment regions. Namely, the length of the path is limited by a budget that can be restored within polytopic replenishment regions. We show that the optimal path in this problem exhibits a distinct geometric structure: it consists of straight-line segments, changes direction at replenishment regions, and visits regions at most once. We propose an approach to solve the continuous problem in two steps: using a graph-based approach, followed by convex programming. First, we define a graph whose nodes are possible waypoints of feasible paths, and the edges are the Euclidean distances between these nodes. To obtain a discrete set of nodes that ensure a feasible and near-optimal solution, we utilize a wavefront algorithm. With a sufficiently small spacing between wavefronts, the solution of the shortest path problem on this graph yields the optimal sequence of polytopes to visit. Next, we use convex optimization on this sequence of polytopes to find the exact optimal path. A numerical experiment is presented to demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach. This approach provides a framework for solving the resource-constrained shortest path with budget reset.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the resource-constrained shortest path problem with budget-reset in polytopic replenishment regions, proving the path's geometric structure (straight-line segments, direction changes at regions, single visits), and proposing a two-step solution combining a graph-based wavefront algorithm for discrete waypoint selection and convex optimization for the exact optimal path.
AI.motivation: To compute the shortest path under resource constraints (budget) where the budget can be restored within polytopic replenishment regions, which has applications in robotics, logistics, and autonomous navigation where vehicles must refuel or recharge.
AI.method: A two-step approach: (1) A graph-based method using a wavefront algorithm to discretize waypoints and determine the optimal sequence of polytopes to visit; (2) Convex programming on this sequence to find the exact optimal path. The graph nodes are possible waypoints with edges representing Euclidean distances.
AI.result: With sufficiently small wavefront spacing, the graph-based solution yields a feasible and near-optimal sequence of polytopes, and subsequent convex optimization finds the exact optimal path. A numerical experiment demonstrates the approach's effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively solves the resource-constrained shortest path problem with budget reset, leveraging the proven geometric structure of optimal paths. The two-step approach provides a practical computational method for continuous path planning under replenishment constraints.

title: Physics-Aware LLM-Based Probabilistic Wind Power Scenario Generation under Extreme Icing Conditions
comment: 5 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables. Accepted by the 2026 IEEE Power & Energy Society General Meeting
summary: Accurately characterizing wind power uncertainty under icing and post-disaster conditions remains a critical challenge for resilient power system operation. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-aware large language model (LLM) framework for probabilistic wind power scenario generation under extreme icing conditions. The proposed framework integrates supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA)-based physical modeling, multimodal tokenization, and a causal Transformer architecture trained in an autoregressive manner. A physics-aware decoding scheme effectively enforces rated power limits and ramping constraints on the generated trajectories while preserving stochastic diversity. Case studies using real wind turbine data show that the proposed method reproduces icing-induced power degradation and temporal variability observed during extreme weather. The resulting scenarios are physically consistent and high-fidelity, thereby significantly enhancing resilience assessment and recovery planning in renewable-integrated power systems.

AI.tldr: A physics-aware LLM framework combining SCADA-based physical modeling, multimodal tokenization, and causal Transformer for probabilistic wind power scenario generation under extreme icing conditions, producing physically consistent and high-fidelity scenarios for resilience assessment.
AI.motivation: Accurately characterizing wind power uncertainty under icing and post-disaster conditions remains a critical challenge for resilient power system operation.
AI.method: Proposes a physics-aware LLM framework integrating SCADA-based physical modeling, multimodal tokenization, and a causal Transformer trained autoregressively, with a physics-aware decoding scheme that enforces rated power limits and ramping constraints while preserving stochastic diversity.
AI.result: Case studies using real wind turbine data show the method reproduces icing-induced power degradation and temporal variability observed during extreme weather; generated scenarios are physically consistent and high-fidelity.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework significantly enhances resilience assessment and recovery planning in renewable-integrated power systems under extreme icing conditions.

title: Dynamic-Key Post-Quantum Encrypted Control Against System Identification Attacks
comment: This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication
summary: This study proposes post-quantum encrypted control systems based on dynamic-key Learning with Errors (LWE) encryption schemes. The proposed method develops update maps that simultaneously update the private key and ciphertexts within the LWE framework, enabling dynamic-key encrypted control resistant to system identification attacks. The growth of errors induced by homomorphic operations is analyzed, and sufficient parameter conditions guaranteeing correct decryption at each control step are clarified. Furthermore, a design procedure for the encrypted control systems is presented based on security metrics such as sample-identifying complexity and deciphering time. A numerical example demonstrates that the proposed control systems achieve secure control against the considered system identification attack.

AI.tldr: Proposes post-quantum encrypted control systems using dynamic-key LWE encryption, with simultaneous key/ciphertext updates to resist system identification attacks, including error growth analysis, decryption guarantees, and a security-based design procedure validated by numerical example.
AI.motivation: To address the vulnerability of encrypted control systems to system identification attacks by developing a post-quantum secure framework with dynamic keys that resist such attacks.
AI.method: Develops update maps for simultaneous private key and ciphertext updates within the LWE framework; analyzes error growth from homomorphic operations; derives sufficient parameter conditions for correct decryption; presents a design procedure based on sample-identifying complexity and deciphering time.
AI.result: The proposed control systems achieve secure control against the considered system identification attack, as demonstrated by a numerical example.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic-key LWE-based encrypted control provides post-quantum security against system identification attacks, with guaranteed correct decryption when parameters satisfy the derived conditions.

title: Unified Energy Function Tailored to Inverter-Based Resources with PI Controllers for Transient Stability Analysis
summary: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) has fundamentally altered the transient stability characteristics of modern power systems. IBRs typically rely on proportional--integral (PI) controllers for synchronization and regulation, resulting in nonlinear swing equations that differ significantly from those of synchronous generators (SGs) and exhibit state-dependent damping. Consequently, although the classical energy function is often adopted in IBR analysis by analogy with SGs, it cannot be directly applied to IBRs with PI controller.
